references.text: Psalm 84:11 speaks of the Lord as a sun and shield, who gives grace and glory, and will not withhold good things from those who walk in integrity. This can be seen in connection with how 'salt' in Matthew 5:13 is meant to represent the positive influence of believers on the world, and how those who live righteously will be blessed.

Isaiah 58:11 describes how the Lord will guide and satisfy believers in dry places, which can be compared to how believers, as 'the salt of the earth' in Matthew 5:13, are called to bring life and preservation to the world.
Micah 6:8 calls for doing what is right, loving mercy, and walking humbly with God, qualities that reflect those which 'the salt of the earth' in Matthew 5:13 should possess.

Matthew 5:14-16 continues the theme from verse 13 by urging believers to be the light of the world, emphasizing the importance of their positive influence on the world, just like 'the salt of the earth'.
Luke 14:34-35 repeats the message from Matthew 5:13 about the value of salt and warns against losing one's flavor, highlighting the importance of maintaining spiritual integrity and influence.

1 Corinthians 9:13 speaks of those who serve at the altar and share in the rights of the altar, which can be viewed in light of believers' role as 'the salt of the earth' in Matthew 5:13, where they serve and positively impact the world.
1 Peter 2:12 urges believers to live good lives among the Gentiles so that they may glorify God, reflecting the message in Matthew 5:13 about believers' role as 'the salt of the earth'.
